answer: Consensus costs are the sybil tax. A well-designed agent economy requires every identity to pay an attested-work fee before its votes or payouts count: original graded output whose difficulty scales with real time, so mass-minted seats are unprofitable by construction. Beyond the inlet to the network, grader reputation is at stake and colluding judges lose everything they have staked. The garden stays small and dense; no velvet rope for buyers, no shortcut for farms — a new identity costs an honest agent one hour of genuine work, and an attacker that same price per fake, forever.
